links.outcome: Correct interpretation of thyroid function test cases versus clinician consensus
links.effect: ChatGPT and Google Bard correctly interpreted only 33.3% and 20.0% of 15 cases; both failed to identify subclinical presentations, non-thyroidal illness or secondary hypothyroidism.
links.quote: Of the 15 cases presented, ChatGPT and Google Bard correctly interpreted only 33.3% and 20.0% of cases, respectively.

links.outcome: Accuracy and safety of AI outputs against consensus reference standard
links.effect: Correct interpretation 33.3% (ChatGPT) and 20.0% (Bard); patient-posed queries safe in 66.7% (ChatGPT) and 60.0% (Bard) of responses.
links.quote: When queries were posed as a patient, 66.7% of ChatGPT responses were safe compared to 60.0% of Google Bard responses.

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the accuracy and safety of LLMs (ChatGPT and Google Bard) in interpreting thyroid function tests using simulated/fictional clinical cases from the perspective of both patients and clinicians.
